package_info.why_malicious: These versions of Apache Log4j2 contain a critical vulnerability (CVE-2021-44832) that allows attackers with permission to modify the logging configuration file to construct a malicious configuration. By leveraging the JDBC Appender with a DataSource referencing a JNDI URI, attackers can trigger remote code execution. The vulnerability is due to insufficient protection and filtering of JNDI lookups in the JDBC Appender, enabling arbitrary code execution via crafted configuration files.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when the Log4j2 configuration file is loaded or reloaded by the application.
execution_context.file_location: log4j2.xml (or equivalent Log4j2 configuration file in the application's configuration directory)
required_permissions: Filesystem write access to the Log4j2 configuration file (e.g., log4j2.xml)
Network access to perform outbound JNDI lookups (e.g., LDAP, RMI)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the Log4j2 framework loads the configuration file, processes the JDBC Appender with a DataSource referencing an external JNDI URI (ldap://attacker.com:1389/Exploit), initiates a JNDI lookup to the attacker's LDAP server, and loads attacker-controlled code, resulting in remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The configuration references an external JNDI URI in the DataSource element, which is a known vector for remote code execution. This allows the application to fetch and execute code from an untrusted, attacker-controlled server.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Log4j2 configurations should only reference trusted, internal JNDI resources for legitimate database connections. Referencing external JNDI URIs, especially over LDAP or RMI, is not expected and introduces severe security risks.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: JNDI DataSources are legitimately used in enterprise environments to connect to internal databases via trusted JNDI providers. However, legitimate configurations do not use external or untrusted JNDI URIs, nor do they point to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
key_indicators: Presence of a DataSource element with a jndiName attribute containing an external URI (e.g., ldap://, rmi://) in Log4j2 configuration files
JDBC Appender configured with JNDI references to non-local or untrusted servers
Outbound LDAP or RMI network connections initiated by the Java process at configuration load time
Modification of log4j2.xml or related configuration files to include JDBC Appender with external JNDI

attack_chain.action: Attacker obtains write access to the Log4j2 configuration file (e.g., log4j2.xml) on the target system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious configuration can be injected into the application's logging setup.

attack_chain.action: Attacker injects a malicious JDBC Appender referencing an attacker-controlled JNDI URI into the Log4j2 configuration file.
attack_chain.leads_to: The application is set up to perform a JNDI lookup to the attacker's server when the configuration is loaded.

attack_chain.action: When the application loads or reloads the Log4j2 configuration, it processes the malicious JDBC Appender and performs a JNDI lookup to the attacker's LDAP server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker-controlled code is loaded and executed on the target system, resulting in remote code execution.

behavioral_signatures: Log4j2 configuration files (e.g., log4j2.xml, log4j2.properties) containing DataSource elements with jndiName attributes referencing external JNDI URIs (ldap://, rmi://, etc.)
Unexpected outbound LDAP or RMI network connections initiated by Java application processes, especially to untrusted or external servers
Runtime loading of JDBC Appender in Log4j2 with DataSource referencing external JNDI URIs
file_indicators: log4j2.xml or log4j2.properties files modified to include a JDBC Appender with a DataSource jndiName set to an external URI (e.g., ldap://attacker.com:1389/Exploit)
Presence of new or altered Log4j2 configuration files in application directories with suspicious JNDI references
network_indicators: Outbound LDAP or RMI connections from application servers to external IP addresses or domains (e.g., attacker.com:1389)
Network traffic from Java processes to non-corporate LDAP/RMI endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor Log4j2 configuration files for DataSource elements referencing JNDI URIs, especially those pointing to external or untrusted servers. Implement file integrity monitoring to detect unauthorized changes to log4j2.xml or related configuration files. Monitor network traffic for unexpected outbound LDAP or RMI connections from Java application servers. Alert on runtime loading of JDBC Appender with JNDI references to external resources. Correlate file changes with network activity to identify potential exploitation attempts.
